content:
A place to return to # I wanted a place that could hold more than a list of links. A personal site is a small promise to pay attention: to write down what I am learning, to keep the useful parts of a project, and to make room for ideas that do not fit neatly into a classroom or a feed.
I am studying electrical engineering at Sharif University of Technology, with a background in astronomy and a continuing interest in mathematics. Those subjects have different vocabularies, but they share a habit I value: start with a question, make the assumptions visible, and keep looking when the first explanation is not enough.
This blog will grow slowly. I expect to write about engineering, astronomy, problem solving, books, and the practical details of building things. The goal is not to sound finished. It is to leave a clear trail of thought that I can follow later, and that might be useful to someone else too.
Thanks for stopping by.
summary: Why I am building a personal site, and what I hope to keep here.

Notes from the workbench # This is where I keep longer thoughts: technical ideas, observations from study, and the occasional detour that turns out to be useful. Some posts will be polished; others will stay closer to a notebook page.
The common thread is curiosity. I am interested in the point where a difficult idea becomes understandable, and in the tools that help us get there.
title: Blog

content:
Hello this is another article from me # Astronomy rewards patience. A point of light can be a planet, a distant star, an instrument artifact, or simply a question waiting for better data. The useful habit is not memorizing every possibility; it is learning to notice what would distinguish one explanation from another.
That habit travels well. In engineering, a circuit that behaves unexpectedly is not being difficult for its own sake. It is telling you that a model, a measurement, or an assumption needs another look.
I am trying to practice that second look more deliberately: slow down, write down what I actually observed, and let the next experiment be smaller and clearer than the last one.
summary: A short note on observation, astronomy, and the value of a second look.

Hello # I am Aria Fateh Kerdari, an electrical engineering student at Sharif University of Technology. I am drawn to problems that sit between precise theory and things you can actually build.
Before engineering became my main home, astronomy gave me a way to think about scale, evidence, and wonder. I was fortunate to earn a gold medal at the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics (IOAA), an experience that still shapes how I learn and collaborate.
What I am exploring # Electrical engineering and the mathematics behind useful systems Astronomy, physics, and the habit of asking better questions Programming as a tool for testing ideas and making them tangible Writing as a way to turn scattered notes into something shareable This site is deliberately simple: a place for finished thoughts, unfinished questions, and the occasional record of how one idea became another.
Say hello # The easiest way to reach me is by email at fatehkerdariaria@gmail.com.
